title: Detect and heal tokenization drift across streaming and batch metering paths
creator: Priya Shah
description: We have recurring discrepancies between billed token counts and what clients observe when requests flow through mixed pipelines (hosted -> dedicated fallback, model family switches, and streaming resume). Root cause hypothesis: inconsistent tokenization and fragment attribution across codepaths (client re-tokenization, model-specific tokenizer differences, streaming resume re-chunking, and retry-induced duplicate/partial attribution). This ticket formalizes detection, reconciliation, and an automated healing path to ensure ledger-correct billing and clear audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic canonical tokenization layer exists for metering that is used to compute billed token counts independent of model-specific tokenizers.
Streaming resume and retry flows include immutable tokenization anchors so resumed fragments map exactly to billed tokens.
Reconciliation job runs nightly and reduces previously-identified billing variance > 95% on sampled accounts (compared to baseline).
New tokenization-drift alerting on billing-mismatch rate > 0.25% for active customers is in place with runbook links.
Backfilled corrections or credit adjustments are generated for affected customers and surfaced to billing/CS as draft adjustments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a long prompt that triggers model fallback mid-stream (hosted -> dedicated) and capture server-side metering events.
2) Simulate a client-side resume where only the last fragment is re-sent with different whitespace (client re-tokenized).
3) Compare billed token tallies from the ledger, the runtime metering events, and a canonical tokenizer run of the final prompt.
4) Observe off-by-one and multi-token drift when model switch or resume happens during multi-byte UTF-8 sequences or with punctuation-normalization differences.
proposed_solution: Introduce a minimal, deterministic canonical tokenization preprocessor in the ingress path that (a) normalizes input unicode/whitespace, (b) produces a canonical token stream used solely for metering, and (c) emits a compact tokenization fingerprint in request metadata. For streaming, extend the resume token to include the last canonical token index and a short VAA (versioned anchor) so resumed fragments can be reconciled without re-tokenizing on the consumer side. Add a nightly reconciliation job that compares canonical-token-attributed usage to ledger entries, highlights anomalies, and optionally emits corrective credit events through the billing pipeline. Instrument end-to-end tests and a synthetic workload generator that exercises model switches, retries, truncation, and multi-region routing to validate correctness across paths.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the canonical tokenizer in ingress; run in shadow mode for 2 weeks while collecting metrics.
Enable resume anchors in streaming with canary on 5% of traffic; monitor duplicate/under-count regression metrics.
Run reconciliation backfill on 30 days of history for a 10% sample of customers to validate correction logic.
Gradually promote to 50% then 100% after 2 successful cycles and postmortem review.
Coordinate with billing and CS teams before issuing any automated credits; initial run will create draft adjustment reports only.
